meta.title: Why should an agent retrieve evidence when its token entropy spikes?

data.command: Why should an agent retrieve evidence when its token entropy spikes?

evidence.text: LOLM-304M beats Pythia-410M on WikiText-103: eval PPL 68.4 vs 142.9 with 26 percent fewer parameters; late-position BPC 1.02 vs 1.23.
The NFET controller maps telemetry (logit entropy, hidden drift, gate mean, regime entropy) to five controls: continue, retrieve, verify, branch, finalize.
High sustained token entropy means the model is uncertain about continuations; retrieving evidence reduces uncertainty better than continuing to guess.
Evaluation practice: match training data and tokenizer, report perplexity windows, late-position bits-per-character, and distinct-n generation diversity.

base.response: When an agent's token entropy spikes, it means the model is uncertain about the next token. Retrieving evidence helps reduce uncertainty by providing more information to guide the agent's decisions. This approach improves the model's ability to make accurate and reliable predictions.
